The royal cemetery of Umm el-Qa’ab near Abydos features the tombs and enclosures of the First Dynasty rulers of Egypt, and dates as far back as 3,000BC.

rfi.title: French PM slams violence at student protests, promises 'timeout' for democracy
rfi.description: French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said there can be "no room for tolerance of violence", as tens of thousands of students took to the streets nationwide on Tuesday to protest over the state of schools. He told parliament that high schools would clear their schedules for the rest of the week to create space for democratic debate and air grievances.

rfi.title: French MEP Hassan under investigation over flag incident at 7 October commemoration
rfi.description: Hard-left French EU lawmaker Rima Hassan is facing an investigation after the Israeli and European Union flags were allegedly thrown to the floor at a commemoration for the 2023 Hamas attacks that set off the Gaza war. Hassan said the action was to denounce the "ongoing genocide by the Israeli government".

rfi.title: EU suspends beef exports from Namibia due to foot and mouth disease
rfi.description: The largest market for Namibian beef, the European Union, announced it has suspended imports after an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, which wreaked havoc in Europe 25 years ago.

rfi.title: France earmarks a further €7m to help fight DRC's worst-ever Ebola crisis
rfi.description: France has decided to allocate an additional €7 million this year to combat the Ebola epidemic currently ravaging the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). This comes as Kenya announced its first-ever death from the disease.

rfi.title: Quebec separatist party wins provincial election in test of Canada's unity
rfi.description: Separatists won provincial elections in Quebec on Monday, with a promise to hold a vote on leaving Canada after US President Donald Trump leaves office, testing Prime Minister Mark Carney's message of national unity.

rfi.title: Tens of thousands expected in Paris for high school protests
rfi.description: Tens of thousands of demonstrators are expected on the streets of Paris on Tuesday as France's powerful trade unions join high school students rallying for better conditions in a wave of protests marked by clashes with police.

rfi.title: Olise strikes twice in France's romp past Belgium in Nations League
rfi.description: Désiré Doué, Ryan Cherki and two goals from Michael Olise launched the late pyrotechnics on Monday night at the Stade de France as France scored four times in 13 minutes to whoosh past Belgium 4-1 and maintain the lead of their Nations League pool.

rfi.title: Lebanon joined by UK and France for three weeks of joint military drills
rfi.description: Lebanon's army will hold three weeks of exercises with the British military from Tuesday, both sides said on Monday, with the drills to involve personnel and representatives from countries including France, Italy and the United States.

rfi.title: Climate change driving child marriages and teen pregnancies, study finds
rfi.description: The charity Plan International said on Monday that global warming has increased the risk of child marriages, teenage pregnancies and violence against girls. Its report coincides with talks in the South Pacific nations of Fiji and Tuvalu, where climate change is affecting all aspects of daily life.

rfi.title: Study shows extreme poverty and homelessness on the rise in France
rfi.description: An international study published on Monday by France’s largest food aid charity, Restos du Cœur, shows the number of people living in extreme poverty in France and other wealthy countries increased by 37 percent between 2018 and 2025.

rfi.title: Chat group kingpin goes on trial in Paris over online abuse of underage girls
rfi.description: A 29-year-old man went on trial on Monday at the Paris Assize Court, charged with running a masculinist chat group on the platform Discord on which young victims were forced to engage in sexual acts online and to mutilate themselves.

rfi.title: Spain PM calls early election after housing crisis defeat
rfi.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday called a snap election for 29 November, after parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government. This comes after tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other cities on Saturday to demand affordable housing.

rfi.title: US-German trio win medicine Nobel for work on optogenetics
rfi.description: The Nobel medicine prize was awarded Monday to US psychiatrist and neurologist Karl Deisseroth and his German colleagues Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their work in the field of optogenetics.

rfi.title: Nobel Prize announcements begin, with hopes of a 'less controversial year'
rfi.description: With this year's Nobel Prize winner announcements beginning on Monday, among those experts believe could be in line for the $1.2 million prizes are GLP-1 researchers, a Ukrainian children's rights activist and several female authors. And after last year's Donald Trump-driven controversy, anticipation around this year's Peace Prize is high.

rfi.title: The pill: from symbol of women's liberation to subject of growing mistrust
rfi.description: Initially a symbol of liberation, the pill went on to become an almost inevitable part of a woman’s contraceptive journey. But today its use in France is in decline, the drop in popularity fuelled by health warnings, mistrust and a changing attitude towards contraception.

rfi.title: Ethiopia captures Tigray capital as its regional rivals meet in Egypt
rfi.description: Ethiopian federal forces have regained control of the Tigray rebels' regional capital, local sources said on Sunday, while Ethiopia's regional rivals gathered in Egypt to discuss the risk of a wider war.

rfi.title: France struggles to fund farm climate adaptation as losses mount
rfi.description: Farmers in France are expecting their first payments shortly under the government's billion-euro emergency aid package to support farmers affected by severe summer heatwaves, droughts and wildfires. As the effects of climate change worsen, experts say compensation alone will not be enough to protect French agriculture in the long term.

rfi.title: Rwandan genocide hunter Dafroza Gauthier dies after long battle for justice
rfi.description: Dafroza Gauthier, who spent spent decades tracking down Rwandans in France accused of involvement in the 1994 genocide, has died from cancer at the age of 72. By filing a string of civil lawsuits against suspected fugitives, she and her husband Alain pushed the French legal system to hold them to account.

euronews.title: Armed Man shot outside Sweden's Royal Palace in Stockholm
euronews.description: Swedish police have shot and wounded an armed man outside the royal palace in central Stockholm. The man has been taken to a hospital.

euronews.title: Judo: Japan crowns two new world champions in Baku
euronews.description: Akari Omori claimed her first world title at -57kg, defeating reigning champion Eteri Liparteliani in golden score. At -73kg, Ryuga Tanaka overcame Makhmadbek Makhmadbekov in a tight final to secure gold and complete a double triumph for Japan.

euronews.title: UK trial of three Iranians over alleged plot to target Iran dissident journalists
euronews.description: In London three Iranians go on trial accused of targeting UK-based journalists opposed to the regime in Tehran

euronews.title: Swedish Patriot missiles to be sent to Poland to bolster NATO's eastern flank
euronews.description: Sweden will send Patriot air-defences and around 100 troops to protect the Rzeszów-Jasionka logistics hub used to route aid to Ukraine. The mission starts on 1 December and will last seven months.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: One student killed, eight wounded in Istanbul school stabbing attack
euronews.description: A 15-year-old student disguised herself in the target school's uniform before attacking pupils at Şeyh Şamil Imam Hatip Secondary School in Başakşehir on Tuesday morning. The suspect, who attends a different school, was apprehended.

euronews.title: Book weighing over 200kg illustrated by Dalí and Cocteau stolen in Auvergne
euronews.description: On the night of 4 to 5 October, the "Book of the Apocalypse", a 210‑kilo volume with works by Salvador Dalí, Jean Cocteau and Bernard Buffet, was stolen from an art centre in Issoire, Puy‑de‑Dôme.

euronews.title: EU-China trade tensions: Five things to know as Brussels and Beijing face crunch talks
euronews.description: The next ten days will be critical for EU-China relations. EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič will travel to Beijing later this week for high-level talks aimed at rebalancing the trade relationship and securing “tangible” results ahead of next week’s meeting of EU leaders.

euronews.title: Brussels eyes agricultural carve-outs from Ukraine's EU membership
euronews.description: The European Commission proposed excluding Ukraine's agricultural products from the EU market and agricultural funding even when Kyiv joins the EU, in a move to smooth the country's accession process and address concerns from several member states.

euronews.title: Russia denies plague death but quarantines hundreds without explanation
euronews.description: Rospotrebnadzor said Darya Shipilova, 28, died of "pneumonia of unknown aetiology" with no links to her work at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Institute, but imposed quarantine on her contacts, confined 60 colleagues inside the facility and restricted access to hospitals including a maternity ward.

euronews.title: 500 arrested as French police clashes with protesters on third day of national action by high school students
euronews.description: Eyewitnesses say police deployed tear gas to quell unrest and disperse crowds in major cities including the capital, Paris, Marseille and Lyon. Officials figures reflected a nationwide participation exceeding a quarter million students in the protests that have rocked Macron's government.

euronews.title: Lithuania takes further step towards lifting nuclear weapons ban
euronews.description: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Tuesday that Lithuania’s move, alongside broader plans to expand US and NATO military infrastructure in the region, risked further escalating tensions.

euronews.title: New EU members face 15-year probation period after joining the bloc
euronews.description: The European Commission is proposing a new procedure to cut funding and voting rights of EU newcomers that breach the rule of law, available for 15 years after accession. The proposal also includes new procedures for the gradual integration of candidate countries and governance measures.

euronews.title: 'Whole world is paying' for Iran war, Qatar warns as mediation efforts continue
euronews.description: The Iran war has disrupted global trade as regional powers prepare to bolster Saudi Arabia’s defences. Qatar said talks to end the war remained active and backed the Mecca defence alliance, but added that it was too early to discuss joining the pact.

euronews.title: EU countries to discuss suspected plague outbreak in Russia
euronews.description: European health authorities are closely following the suspected plague outbreak in Siberia, Russia. The European Commission and member states are set to discuss the matter on Wednesday morning.

euronews.title: Metsola to take action after MEP Rima Hassan removes Israeli flag
euronews.description: French pro-Palestinian MEP Rima Hassan removed Israeli and EU flags from an exhibition commemorating the victims of Hamas’s 7 October terrorist attack, sparking outrage among fellow lawmakers. She could face a suspension of her daily allowance.

euronews.title: EU Commission throws down the gauntlet to member states on reforming the bloc
euronews.description: The European Commission is proposing fewer commissioners and less unanimity to prepare the EU for 30 or more members. However, EU diplomats say capitals are unlikely to agree.

euronews.title: Two Spanish F-18 jets scrambled in Romania after drone alert near Ukraine
euronews.description: Two Spanish F-18s deployed in Romania under NATO command took off at dawn after two air targets were detected near the Ukrainian border. The objects did not ultimately enter Romanian airspace and were not intercepted.

lemonde.title: Mouvement lycéen : Sébastien Lecornu sous la pression de la rue, des oppositions et d’Emmanuel Macron
lemonde.description: Alors que des milliers de manifestants défilaient dans toute la France, mardi, en soutien à la mobilisation des lycéens, le premier ministre s’est exprimé pour la première fois depuis le début de cette crise sociale. Face aux députés, il a défendu le déploiement d’un important dispositif policier et pris pour cible La France insoumise.

lemonde.title: Au Mali, la junte regagne du terrain en reprenant Kidal, fief des rebelles touareg
lemonde.description: Les militaires maliens et leurs alliés russes avaient été chassés de la ville du Nord le 25 avril, durant l’offensive conjointe des indépendantistes du Front de libération de l’Azawad et des djihadistes du Groupe de soutien de l’islam et des musulmans.

lemonde.title: Allemagne : l’affaire August Hanning, l’ancien chef des services secrets soupçonné d’espionnage, illustre les failles de l’agence du renseignement extérieur
lemonde.description: L’ancien responsable du BND, âgé de 80 ans, aurait continué à recevoir des informations confidentielles bien après son départ en 2005, et est accusé d’en avoir transmis certaines à une puissance étrangère. Il a été arrêté à son domicile.

lemonde.title: Dans un contexte de guerre commerciale avec la Chine, l’arsenal de l’Europe se renforce
lemonde.description: L’Union européenne dispose déjà de nombreux instruments pour défendre ses industries face à la concurrence chinoise. Paris et Berlin appellent la Commission à les utiliser plus amplement et à les renforcer.

lemonde.title: Les exportations de pétrole du Golfe rebondissent au-delà de leurs niveaux d’avant-guerre
lemonde.description: Malgré l’augmentation des flux de brut en provenance du Moyen-Orient, la pénurie croissante de navires pétroliers est en train de créer un nouveau goulet d’étranglement.

lemonde.title: Ecrits antisémites : l’affaire Jordan Bardella plombe la séquence budgétaire du RN
lemonde.description: Poursuivant sa stratégie de déni, le président du Rassemblement national a dû répondre, aux côtés de Marine Le Pen, aux questions des journalistes, lors d’une conférence de presse organisée pour présenter la trajectoire budgétaire de la candidate en cas de victoire à l’élection présidentielle.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : pour les candidats, la difficulté de mener campagne alors que plane la menace d’une crise financière et budgétaire
lemonde.description: Matignon prévient qu’une aggravation du déficit pourrait entraver l’action du prochain chef de l’Etat. Dans ce climat anxiogène, les prétendants à l’Elysée s’opposent sur les solutions à apporter.

lemonde.title: Christa Pike, dont la mise à mort avait échoué aux Etats-Unis, a repris connaissance et parle

lemonde.title: Orages, pluie et inondations : le Gard, l’Hérault, les Bouches-du-Rhône et le Var en vigilance orange mercredi
lemonde.description: « Les orages sont également susceptibles de donner, outre une forte activité électrique, de la grêle et des rafales de vent, voire des phénomènes tourbillonnaires en zones littorales », fait savoir Météo-France dans son bulletin mercredi matin.

lemonde.title: « Un mélange hétérogène de délires complotistes » : sept ans de prison requis contre Rémy Daillet
lemonde.description: Pour le parquet national antiterroriste, l’instigateur de l’enlèvement de la petite Mia, également soupçonné d’avoir fomenté un coup d’Etat à la tête d’un groupuscule d’ultradroite, est toujours « incapable de la moindre autocritique ».

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : une attaque de drones ukrainiens déclenche un vaste incendie sur un pétrolier au large de Sotchi, en Russie
lemonde.description: Des images largement diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux montrent d’importantes flammes en mer et une épaisse colonne de fumée s’élevant dans le ciel. En raison de l’intensité du sinistre, les pompiers n’ont pas pu intervenir, mais un équipage de 23 personnes a été secouru, selon le ministère des transports russe.

lemonde.title: Le prêtre Jean-Bernard Plessy, ancien directeur des Chartreux à Lyon, mis en examen pour viol aggravé
lemonde.description: Selon l’avocate de la plaignante, une jeune étudiante, les « violences dénoncées ont persisté durant plusieurs mois, jusqu’en juillet ».

lemonde.title: En Cisjordanie occupée, un photojournaliste de l’Agence France-Presse roué de coups par des colons israéliens
lemonde.description: Jaafar Ashtiyeh, photographe palestinien de 58 ans, a été blessé à la tête et au torse et a été emmené à l’hôpital en ambulance, selon l’agence de presse internationale. Son directeur de l’information, Phil Chetwynd, dénonce « une attaque grave » et « inacceptable ».

lemonde.title: En Australie, la justice s’oppose à l’extension d’une mine de charbon
lemonde.description: Dans un arrêt prononcé mercredi, la Haute Cour australienne s’oppose à un vaste plan d’extension d’une mine de charbon à ciel ouvert, au nord de Sydney, en raison des conséquences climatiques du projet. Une victoire pour les militants écologistes.

lemonde.title: Mort de l’actrice américaine Eva Marie Saint
lemonde.description: La comédienne, décédée à l’âge de 102 ans, avait eu l’Oscar de la meilleure actrice dans un second rôle pour sa prestation dans « Sur les quais », d’Elia Kazan, en 1954.

lemonde.title: Air France-KLM met en avant ses retombées économiques en Europe, à la veille de la décision finale sur la privatisation de TAP Air Portugal
lemonde.description: La compagnie franco-néerlandaise aurait engendré 113 milliards d’euros de richesse produite dans l’Union européenne en 2025 et contribué à créer 1,2 million d’emplois directs et indirects, selon une étude économique publiée mardi.

zeit.title: 1. FC Nürnberg: Wie Miro Klose einen Traditionsverein belebt
zeit.description: Mein ehemaliger Mitspieler setzt auf Jugend, wahrt Hierarchien und verzichtet auf taktische Überfrachtung. So führt er den 1. FC Nürnberg zurück in Richtung Bundesliga.

zeit.title: Wetter: Einmal noch Sonne - danach ziehen Regenwolken auf
Schulwahl: Wie finde ich die richtige Schule für mein Kind?
zeit.description: Kaum etwas stresst Eltern so sehr, wie die Wahl der richtigen weiterführenden Schule für ihr Kind. Eine Lehrerin erklärt, worauf man wirklich achten muss.

zeit.title: Bafög-Reform: »So ist das Studium kein Privileg, sondern handfeste Armut«
zeit.description: 82 Prozent der alleinlebenden Studierenden sind arm, zeigt eine neue Studie. Eine der Autorinnen erklärt, was das mit Mietwuchern und verschleppten Reformen zu tun hat.

zeit.title: Hackerangriff auf Solaranlagen: Deutschland war nur einen Knopfdruck vom Superblackout entfernt
zeit.description: Ein Hacker hätte Hunderttausende Solaranlagen abschalten und so einen großflächigen Stromausfall verursachen können. Zum Glück war es einer von den Guten. Dieses Mal.

zeit.title: Babyleichen: Polizei hofft auf neue Hinweise zu Babyleichen-Fall
Wetterbericht: Wann es heute im Südwesten gewittern könnte
Dritter Jahrestag des Hamas-Angriffs vom 7. Oktober: Gedenkveranstaltungen und Proteste in Berlin geplant
zeit.description: Zum Jahrestag des Hamas-Angriffs auf Israel sind auch in Deutschland Veranstaltungen angesetzt. Im Bundestag findet eine Debatte zu Antisemitismus statt. Das Liveblog

zeit.title: Mehr Fälle: Kindesmissbrauch mit KI: Cyber-Ermittler vor neuen Problemen
Umfrage: Sorgen um Geld – Frauen fühlen sich finanziell unsicherer
Zalando Erfurt: Nach dem Zalando-Aus startet die Jobvermittlung
Bundesgerichtshof: Spionageverdacht: Kommt Ex-BND-Chef Hanning in U-Haft?
Neue Sperrungen: Umleitungen und Ersatzbusse: Bahn sperrt Strecke in Duisburg
Russland: WHO fordert Transparenz nach Tod von Laborantin in Russland
zeit.description: Der WHO-Chef verlangt einen Informationsaustausch zu dem angeblichen Lungenpestfall in Russland. Man müsse widersprüchliche Berichte klären, um Gefahren einzuschätzen.

zeit.title: Dritter Jahrestag des 7. Oktober: Bundesregierung bekennt sich zum Kampf gegen Antisemitismus
zeit.description: Deutschland stehe fest an Israels Seite, sagt der Bundeskanzler vor dem dritten Jahrestag des 7. Oktober. Außenminister Johann Wadephul warnt vor Judenhass.

nzz.title: DER ANDERE BLICK - Die CDU muss sich neu erfinden. Ob das gelingt, ist fraglich
nzz.description: Die deutsche Kanzlerpartei ist im freien Fall. Der Kredit, den die Christlichdemokraten in der Bevölkerung hatten, ist aufgebraucht.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Drei Jahre nach dem Terror vom 7. Oktober: Aus den Opfern wurden Angeklagte
nzz.description: Militärisch hat die Hamas ihren Krieg gegen Israel verloren. Politisch hat die Terrorgruppe ihr Ziel erreicht – auch dank treuen Verbündeten im Westen.

nzz.title: Wenn sogar Nobelpreisträger mit KI schreiben
nzz.description: Der Literaturbetrieb hat seine ersten Skandale wegen der Nutzung von künstlicher Intelligenz. Das beschäftigt auch die Frankfurter Buchmesse. Braucht es überhaupt noch einen Autor?

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - Am 7. Oktober 2023 wurden sie verschleppt – heute ist für sie jeder Moment in Freiheit kostbar
nzz.description: Sie wurden verschleppt und Wochen, Monate oder Jahre festgehalten – in Häusern ihrer Entführer oder in Tunneln der Hamas, während über ihnen der Krieg tobte. Drei Jahre nach dem 7. Oktober geben ehemalige israelische Geiseln Einblick in ihr Leben nach der Gefangenschaft.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Englands Grüne zeigen ihr wahres Gesicht: Sie erklären Zionismus zum Rassismus
nzz.description: An ihrer Parteikonferenz hat die Partei für eine Motion gestimmt, die Israel das Existenzrecht abspricht. Sie bestätigt damit, was man schon lange vermutete: Sie hält nichts von einer Heimstatt für die Juden.

nzz.title: Machtkampf an den Finanzmärkten: Die steigenden Anleiherenditen könnten die Aktienkurse bald in die Knie zwingen
nzz.description: Immer wieder einmal scheinen sich Anleihe- und Aktienmärkte zu widersprechen. Was können Anleger aus der Historie lernen?

nzz.title: «Nie mehr Orban»: Die EU-Kommission droht künftigen Mitgliedstaaten mit Stimmrechtsentzug bei Verstössen
nzz.description: Die EU soll bald anwachsen. Mit Schutzmassnahmen versucht die Erweiterungskommissarin Marta Kos, Skeptiker in Westeuropa zu beschwichtigen. Diese fürchten sich etwa vor ukrainischem Getreide.

nzz.title: Welcher Bolsonaro würde Brasilien denn nun regieren?
nzz.description: Flávio Bolsonaro geht als Erstplatzierter in die Stichwahl. Doch sollte er Präsident werden, dürfte sein Vater der mächtigste Bolsonaro bleiben.

nzz.title: Wie extreme Linke und Terrorsympathisanten die Schülerproteste in Frankreich unterwandern
nzz.description: Die Linkspopulisten von Jean-Luc Mélenchon setzen bei den Präsidentschaftswahlen auf junge Wähler. Dafür sind sie bereit, Gewalt zu legitimieren. Profitieren könnte am Ende die extreme Rechte.

nzz.title: Vertriebene Fussballklubs und lange Anreisen für Fans: So hält Israel den Ligabetrieb aufrecht
nzz.description: Die Raketen auf das Stadion drängen einen Profiklub ins Exil.Drei Jahre nach dem Angriff der Hamas am 7. Oktober prägt das Gedenken an die Opfer auch den israelischen Fussball.

nzz.title: Der neue Peugeot E-208 GTi fordert seine Konzernbrüder heraus
nzz.description: Breiter, tiefer und 281 PS stark: Der E-208 GTi bringt echtes Gokart-Gefühl zurück, fordert beim Laden aber Geduld.

nzz.title: Wann soll Schluss sein mit lebensverlängernden Therapien? Eine Annäherung mit Ärzten und Ethikern
nzz.description: Wegen der steigenden Krankenkassenprämien flammt die Debatte über den Verzicht auf Behandlungen im hohen Alter neu auf. Doch das ist ethisch heikel.

nzz.title: Zürichs ältester Antiquar: «Bücher sind eine Lebenshilfe»
nzz.description: Seit fast fünfzig Jahren führt Armin Trösch sein liebenswertes Zürcher Antiquariat. Doch finanzielle Sorgen belasten sein Lebenswerk. Und kürzlich erschwerte ein brutaler Überfall seine Lage.

nzz.title: Trägt Netanyahu eine Mitschuld am 7. Oktober? Eine Wahrheitssuche drei Jahre danach
nzz.description: Neue Recherchen bekräftigen einen alten Verdacht: Israels Ministerpräsident soll Warnungen vor einem Angriff der Hamas erhalten haben. Doch solange er regiert, bleibt eine schonungslose Aufarbeitung illusorisch.

nzz.title: Chat-GPT geht auf die Finanzbranche los: Verlieren die «Finance Bros» nun ihre Jobs?
nzz.description: Open AI hat einen KI-Agenten lanciert, der viele Aufgaben von Finanzleuten übernehmen kann. Besonders für Berufseinsteiger sind das schlechte Nachrichten.

nzz.title: Der USA-Chef von Bayer warnt davor, dass die Amerikaner die Medikamentenforschung der Welt nicht mehr subventionieren wollen: «Wir stehen am Beginn einer Neuordnung»
nzz.description: Sebastian Guth hat die Pharmasparte des deutschen Traditionskonzerns in den USA seit 2018 stark ausgebaut. Trotz Trumps Druck auf die Branche hat er grosse Wachstumspläne für das Land.

france24fr.title: En direct - Yémen : les Houthis attaquent l'aéroport d'Aden avec des drones et des missiles
france24fr.description: L'aéroport international d'Aden, ville où siège le gouvernement du Yémen internationalement reconnu, a été attaqué par les Houthis à l'aide de missiles et de drones, a annoncé mercredi l'agence de presse gouvernementale Saba. La coalition militaire menée par l'Arabie saoudite avait dit un peu plus tôt avoir intercepté au nord de Ryad un missile balistique tiré par les Houthis. En Israël, la journée sera marquée par les commémorations les trois ans des attaques du 7-Octobre. Notre direct.

france24fr.title: Gratitude et nostalgie en Argentine : Lionel Messi a fait ses adieux à l'Albiceleste
france24fr.description: Lionel Messi a disputé mardi son tout dernier match avec l'Albiceleste devant plus de 80 000 spectateurs au Monumental de Buenos Aires, marquant un dernier but face au Bénin. L'octuple Ballon d'or, 126 buts et 208 sélections, a eu l'occasion de remercier chaudement ses supporters, déjà nostalgiques.

france24fr.title: Trois ans après, Israël commémore les attaques du 7-Octobre juste avant les élections
france24fr.description: Plusieurs cérémonies sont prévues ce mercredi en Israël, trois ans après les attaques du 7-Octobre perpétrées par le Hamas. Ces commémorations se déroulent dans un état d'alerte accrue, à trois semaines des élections législatives.

france24fr.title: En Haïti, les autorités annoncent le report sine die des élections présidentielle et législatives
france24fr.description: Face aux violences des gangs, les autorités électorales d'Haïti ont annoncé mardi reporter sine die les élections présidentielle et législatives qui auraient dû avoir lieu en décembre.

france24fr.title: Comment le 7-Octobre a transformé Israël
france24fr.description: Trois ans, jour pour jour, après les attaques du 7-Octobre, Israël n'est plus le même pays. Pendant près de deux ans, l'état hébreu a vécu au rythme des otages. Mais ces attaques terroristes du Hamas ont aussi bouleversé le rapport des Israéliens à leur armée et à leurs dirigeants.

france24fr.title: États-Unis : après son exécution ratée, Christa Pike a "repris connaissance et peut parler"
france24fr.description: Près d'une semaine après avoir survécu à deux injections létales dans le Tennessee, la condamnée à mort Christa Pike " a repris connaissance et peut parler", ont annoncé ses avocats mardi. Ils n'ont cependant pas été autorisés à lui rendre visite à l'hôpital.

france24fr.title: Le Renseignement allemand dans la tourmente après l'arrestation pour espionnage d'un ancien chef
france24fr.description: August Hanning, qui a dirigé le Renseignement allemand de 1998 à 2005, est soupçonné d'avoir utilisé des documents classés secrets pour rédiger une analyse destiné à un service de renseignement étranger, possiblement azerbaïdjanais, selon Der Spiegel. C'est son ancien directeur de cabinet, en poste jusqu'en 2006, qui est suspecté d'avoir transmis les documents. L'annonce, mardi, de l'arrestation des deux hommes, embarrasse les services allemands qui cherchent à se renforcer face à la Russie.

france24fr.title: Blocage des lycées en France : l'armée en renfort ?
france24fr.description: Les manifestations de lycéens et les blocages d'établissements de ces derniers jours en France ont donné lieu à des affrontements entre élèves et forces de l'ordre : un contexte de violence propice pour véhiculer l'idée que l'armée pourrait venir réprimer le mouvement de contestation.

france24fr.title: Un kenyan venant de République démocratique du Congo décède du virus Ebola
france24fr.description: Pour la toute première fois le Kenya pays enregistre un cas du virus. Un homme d’affaire kenyan de 40 ans a voyagé depuis la RDC vers l’Ouganda avant de prendre l’avion vers Nairobi. Il était contaminé et présentait des symptômes depuis plusieurs semaines. Il est décédé hier à Nairobi où les autorités sont en alerte et font le maximum pour tenter d’empêcher que la maladie ne se répande dans la capitale.

france24fr.title: Manifestation des lycéens : les messages derrière leurs pancartes
france24fr.description: Les lycéens français ont fait entendre leurs revendications lors de manifestations dans toute la France, mardi 6 octobre, avec l'intention affichée de poursuivre leur mobilisation. Nos journalistes présents dans le cortège parisien se sont entretenus eux.

france24fr.title: Cristiano Ronaldo s'excuse et ouvre la porte à un retour en sélection portugaise
france24fr.description: Une semaine après avoir claqué la porte de la sélection portugaise, Cristiano Ronaldo a présenté ses excuses mardi et a ouvert la porte à un retour "après avoir purgé la suspension" qui lui sera appliquée.

france24fr.title: Trump fragilise-t-il son camp ?
france24fr.description: À moins d’un mois des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis, Donald Trump multiplie les déplacements pour reprendre la main sur la campagne, alors que sa popularité est au plus bas. Les républicains pourraient perdre la chambre des représentants mais aussi le sénat. Pouvoir d’achat, inégalités de richesse et investissements dans l’intelligence artificielle s’imposent au cœur des préoccupations des Américains. Une campagne décisive pour Donald Trump et son parti.

france24fr.title: En Syrie, plus de 2 000 proches de jihadistes toujours aux mains des Kurdes
france24fr.description: Quelque 2 200 proches de jihadistes présumés d'une cinquantaine de nationalités se trouvent toujours dans un camp du nord-est de la Syrie sous le contrôle des Kurdes malgré un accord d'intégration des institutions kurdes au sein de l'État syrien.

france24fr.title: Santé: les diverses pollutions de l'alimentation en France
france24fr.description: La cellule investigation de Radio France et du réseau ICI a fait analyser des œufs de poules élevées en plein air aux 4 coins de l'Hexagone. 60% étaient contaminés aux polluants éternels. Un nouvel exemple des pollutions qui touchent l'alimentation des Français. Après de nombreuses alertes des autorités sanitaires, des mesures ont enfin été prises pour limiter progressivement le cadmium dans les engrais. Mais dans le même temps plusieurs pesticides jusque là interdits ont été réautorisés.

france24fr.title: L’avenir de Parcoursup, une question au cœur des revendications lycéennes
france24fr.description: La plateforme d’affectation des futurs étudiants de l’enseignement supérieur, Parcoursup, fait l’objet de critiques récurrentes depuis son lancement en 2018. Sa suppression ou sa refonte sont au cœur des revendications du mouvement lycéen, qui a réuni mardi 450 000 manifestants dans les rues, selon ses organisateurs.

france24fr.title: Une pré-COP Climat aux Fidji, pays menacé par la montée des eaux
france24fr.description: Une pré-COP climat se déroule cette semaine aux Fidji, archipel menacé par la montée des eaux. Les pays insulaires, qui jouent leur survie, veulent peser davantage sur les négociations climatiques. Leur principal objectif: stopper le réchauffement à 1,5°C maximum. D'ici 2050, 1 milliards 200 millions de personnes pourraient être contraintes à l'exil en raison de la montée du niveau des océans.

france24fr.title: La mobilisation lycéenne en France très suivie aux États-Unis
france24fr.description: La mobilisation des lycéens en France est très suivie à l'étranger, notamment aux États-Unis. C'est en une des sites du New York Times, du Wall Street journal, de CNN... Analyse de Matthieu Mabin, correspondant de France 24 à Washington.

france24fr.title: Mobilisation étudiante : premiers heurts dans le cortège parisien
france24fr.description: La place de la République à Paris était noire de monde en début d'après-midi. Des milliers de jeunes s'y sont retrouvés à 14 heures pour “l'acte III” de leur mobilisation. Les lycéens, soutenus par les syndicats, appellent à faire grève pour dénoncer plusieurs difficultés : des établissements dégradés, des professeurs absents, la plateforme Parcoursup… Sur place, quelques tensions avec la police ont été remontées. Notre reporter Pauline Godart est sur le terrain.

observador.title: As notícias das 4h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: 3h. Leonel Messi despede-se da seleção argetina
observador.description: Perante cerca de 85 mil pessoas, Messi foi homenageado antes, durante e depois do jogo. Ainda, Governo francês prepara regresso à normalidade nas escolas depois de dias de protestos.

observador.title: 2h. OMS pede transparência à Rússia perante caso de peste
observador.description: O diretor-geral da OMS pede comunicação “oportuna e transparente”. Ainda neste jornal, Cristiano Ronaldo pede desculpa por ter abandonado a equipa e diz estar disponível como sempre para Portugal.

observador.title: 1h. França prepara regresso à normalidade após protestos
observador.description: Ministério da Educação francês deu instruções para a reabertura gradual das escolas a partir de quarta.  Ainda, PS confirma que vai viabilizar Orçamento do Estado para evitar "precipício político".

observador.title: Seis pilares, 17 medidas e um timing que até calhou bem
observador.description: Movimento Unum teve primeiro evento público com sala cheia e discutiu durante duas horas reformas para arbitragem nacional que serão agora entregues à Direção: "São os nossos dirigentes que decidem".

observador.title: Cristiano Ronaldo quebrou o silêncio. E agora? - EXTRA
observador.description: Quase uma semana depois do abandono da seleção, Cristiano Ronaldo emitiu um comunicado a contar a sua versão do que aconteceu. Bruno Roseiro é o convidado.

observador.title: IL Porto. Parecer por 40 segundos e conflito de interesses
observador.description: Apesar de pedido de presidente da mesa e candidata sobre lista apresentada depois da hora, Conselho de Jurisdição deu luz verde e recusa "exclusão assente num formalismo tecnológico de segundos".

observador.title: Cooperativa de habitação reclama crédito do Banco de Fomento
observador.description: Em junho, o Banco de Fomento anunciou 500 milhões para financiar cooperativas. Meses depois, as linhas de crédito continuam por lançar e os projetos em espera, denuncia a cooperativa A Casa.

observador.title: Morreu Eva Marie Saint, ícone da era dourada de Hollywood
observador.description: Ganhou o Óscar pelo trabalho ao lado de Marlon Brando e Elia Kazan e rompeu o estereótipo da "loira sedutora" no trabalho com Hitchcock. Afastou-se do estrelato, mas passou pela televisão.

observador.title: Israel, onde o Ocidente começa
observador.description: Muitos, na Europa, um dia deveriam perceber as consequências da vulgarização dos termos “fascista” ou “genocídio.”  É, simultaneamente, a vulgarização do mal e a incapacidade de ver o mal absoluto.

observador.title: É o dinheiro, estúpido
observador.description: Quando falamos em reparações, nunca nos devemos esquecer do seu preço e do que os reparacionistas acima de tudo querem: dinheiro.

observador.title: O sanchismo, doença infantil do esquerdismo espanhol
observador.description: Um governante que, depois de derrotado, se agarra a um alçapão institucional para impor o que as Cortes recusaram está a usurpar o poder.

observador.title: Jesus ou Cristiano? Escolho vem aí o diabo
observador.description: Giro, ver tanta da malta que acha condição suficiente para ser português aparecer na AIMA em dia à escolha das 9 às 17, tão empolgada na defesa do que crê ser o superior interesse da Seleção Nacional.

observador.title: Mulher morre atropelada por camião em Estremoz
observador.description: O alerta foi dado às 15h58. A vítima foi transportada em estado grave para o centro de saúde local, onde acabou por não resistir aos ferimentos.

observador.title: Ronaldo
observador.description: Às vezes, há coisas para a gente rir. O nosso primeiro correu para o telefone com o louvável propósito de sanar o conflito.

observador.title: O partido que não existe e ganhou a primeira volta
observador.description: O PT passou vinte anos a ensinar o Brasil a votar contra alguém. O Brasil aprendeu a lição.

observador.title: Peão atropelado na A22 em estado grave
observador.description: O homem despistou-se no sentido Portimão-Lagos, saltou o separador e foi colhido no sentido contrário. Foi levado para o Hospital de Portimão.

observador.title: Leão rugiu no deserto
observador.description: Num tempo dominado pela polarização ideológica, o Papa não vem propor mais uma ideologia, mas uma presença: Jesus Cristo, presente hoje.

spiegel.title: Mareike Fallwickl: Was lernt der »Angry Female Club« im Roman »Haltet euch fest«?
News: Umfrage sieht Merz gescheitert, Gedenken an Hamas-Opfer vom 7. Oktober, Galeria-Insolvenz
spiegel.description: Der Kanzler ist nach Ansicht der Deutschen gescheitert. Am dritten Jahrestag trauern wir um die Opfer des Terrorangriffs vom 7. Oktober. Und Galeria darf nicht sterben! Das ist die Lage am Mittwochmorgen.

spiegel.title: Immobilien: Wie Sie verklausulierte Formulierungen in Anzeigen richtig deuten
spiegel.description: Liebhaberobjekt, gepflegt und lichtdurchflutet – das klingt erst mal toll, sollte Sie aber skeptisch machen. Hier erfahren Sie, worauf Sie bei Immobilienanzeigen achten müssen.

spiegel.title: Haus oder ETF: Immobilien-Trick als Alternative zum MSCI World?
spiegel.description: Ein Haus oder eine Wohnung kosten oft mehr, als sich viele leisten können. Mit einem Kredithebel kann das aber zum Vorteil werden. Wann die Strategie attraktiv sein kann, und warum sie in der Praxis häufig scheitert.

spiegel.title: Soziale Medien: Jeremy Allen White bremst seinen App-Konsum aus
spiegel.description: TikTok, Instagram und Co. können Zeit und Hirnzellen rauben. Das hat auch Schauspieler Jeremy Allen White festgestellt. Er verrät eine Methode, mit der er sich das Scrollen vermiest.

spiegel.title: NBA: Saison-Aus für Ariel Hukporti nach schwerer Verletzung
spiegel.description: Schon die TV-Bilder ließen wenig Gutes vermuten. Und tatsächlich ist die Diagnose für Ariel Hukporti niederschmetternd. Der frischgebackene NBA-Meister fällt schwer verletzt lange aus.

spiegel.title: Eva Marie Saint: Oscarpreisträgerin mit 102 Jahren gestorben
spiegel.description: Sie arbeitete mit den Größten der Branche, holte gleich mit ihrer ersten Rolle einen Academy-Award – und stand noch im greisen Alter vor der Kamera. Nun ist Schauspielerin Eva Marie Saint gestorben.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: US-Präsident will Wladimir Putin wegen Pestverdacht in Russland anrufen
spiegel.description: Die russischen Behörden wiegeln zwar ab. Doch der mutmaßliche Pest-Tod einer Laborangestellten in Sibirien beschäftigt auch das Weiße Haus. Donald Trump will persönlich im Kreml nachfragen.

spiegel.title: Cristiano Ronaldo erklärt Abreise und erhebt Vorwürfe gegen Coach Jorge Jesus
spiegel.description: Seine Abreise von der Nationalmannschaft brachte den Eklat – nun erklärt sich Fußballidol Cristiano Ronaldo. Was er über Portugals Coach Jorge Jesus zu sagen hat, dürfte die Lage aber kaum entschärfen.

spiegel.title: Tennessee: Christa Pike ist nach missglückter Hinrichtung wieder bei Bewusstsein
spiegel.description: Die zum Tode verurteilte Mörderin Christa Pike ist US-Medien zufolge wieder bei Bewusstsein und ansprechbar. Ihre missglückte Hinrichtung hatte für Empörung gesorgt.

spiegel.title: CDU-Politiker fordert höhere Erbschaftsteuer
spiegel.description: »Leistung muss mehr zählen als Herkunft«: Der Vorsitzende der Arbeitnehmergruppe in der Unionsfraktion, Stefan Nacke, plädiert laut »SZ« für eine höhere Erbschaftsteuer – und weicht damit deutlich von der Parteilinie ab.

spiegel.title: Berlin: Prominente von CDU, Grünen und SPD warnen vor Rot-Grün-Rot
spiegel.description: Joschka Fischer, Wolfgang Thierse, Peter Altmaier: Dutzende bekannte Stimmen sprechen sich in einem Appell gegen eine Regierung von Linken, Grünen und SPD in Berlin aus. Die Vorsondierungen gehen derweil weiter.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt: Wo kommen die CDU-Stimmen für die AfD her?
spiegel.description: Deutschlands erster AfD-Landtagspräsident erhielt vier Stimmen mehr, als AfD und BSW Sitze im Landtag von Magdeburg haben. Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen wird unter Christdemokraten nach den Schuldigen gesucht.

spiegel.title: Cornell: Juristin Sally Yates soll Umgang der Universität mit »Jane Doe«-Fall prüfen
spiegel.description: Welche Fehler hat die US-Eliteuniversität Cornell im Fall der mutmaßlichen Vergewaltigung von »Jane Doe« gemacht? Das soll nun Sally Yates untersuchen – bekannt aus ihrem Spitzenjob in den Obama-Jahren.

spiegel.title: Karl Bushby: Nach 28 Jahren kehrt der Weltumwanderer nach England zurück
spiegel.description: 50.000 Kilometer legte er zurück: Der Brite Karl Bushby ist Jahrzehnte nach seinem Start in Patagonien nun in seiner Heimat angekommen – indem er den Ärmelkanal durchschwamm. Am Strand erwarteten ihn sein Vater und Werner Herzog.

spiegel.title: August Hanning: Festnahme des Ex-BND-Chefs erschüttert Sicherheitsapparat
spiegel.description: Die Festnahme von Ex-BND-Chef August Hanning ist ein Schock für den deutschen Sicherheitsapparat. Dabei waren seine dubiosen Beratergeschäfte seit Jahren bekannt. Hätte die Regierung früher einschreiten können? Die SPIEGEL-Rekonstruktion.

spiegel.title: Debatte in Israel: Wer trägt die Verantwortung für das FlyDubai-Desaster?

phys-org.description: Physicist Francis Halzen has an impressively long list of academic accolades—but every October, as the Nobel Prize rolled around, his failure to bag the biggest award of them all left him "miserable," he admits.

phys-org.title: Computer scientist tracks satellites with automated observatory built from off-the-shelf technology
phys-org.description: Allen Schnibben's interest in space started when he was a child. "I picked up some books about the solar system when I was in elementary school. In middle school, I got a telescope and I started observing the night sky as a hobby," said Schnibben, a computer scientist at Sandia National Laboratories. "My entire life, I've had an interest in space." Now, Schnibben collects data on satellites at Sandia's SOHBRIT facility, a 12-foot-wide (3.7-meter-wide) observatory.

phys-org.title: Study highlights the European waters at greatest risk of harmful light pollution
phys-org.description: Scientists have produced a first-of-its-kind assessment showing which coastal regions of Europe they believe are at greatest risk from harmful light pollution.

phys-org.title: 'Quiet firing' linked to higher levels of 'quiet quitting' among employees
phys-org.description: A study of the oil, gas and petroleum industry has found that "quiet firing" by employers is associated with higher levels of "quiet quitting" among employees, while strong workplace relationships can weaken that effect. The research appears in the International Journal of Business Information Systems.

phys-org.title: Linguists find Madonna's voice defies age-related expectations
phys-org.description: As women go through menopause, their voices tend to become deeper. This is partly because the vocal folds may swell and the surrounding muscles lose elasticity, resulting in a lower pitch. Age-related physiological changes can also affect the pronunciation of certain vowels.

phys-org.title: Nearly 10,000 mapped reactions reveal overlooked steps in CO₂-to-fuel conversion
phys-org.description: Scientists are increasingly exploring carbon dioxide (CO₂) hydrogenation—where CO₂ reacts with hydrogen over a catalyst to produce products like methanol—to convert CO₂ into useful chemicals and fuels. However, it involves thousands of tiny chemical steps happening on the catalyst surface.

phys-org.title: Sorghum may help European agriculture face climate change
phys-org.description: Research by INRAE and AgroParisTech suggests that global warming could have an overall positive effect on sorghum yields in Europe. Sorghum is a promising alternative to maize in livestock feed. Additionally, the crop requires less water and can tolerate higher temperatures. The researchers carried out simulations that used past climate data and future climate scenarios with the broader goal of developing new strategies for European agriculture. phys-org.title: New crocodile species discovered in rocks used to build the Great Sphinx
phys-org.description: A new species of extinct crocodile from Egypt has been discovered, sharing more than just its home with the Great Sphinx. Herugavialis cairensis was found in the very same rocks used to build the iconic monument. And, just as the Sphinx is famously missing the tip of its nose, the fossil crocodile is also missing the tip of its snout.

phys-org.title: From coral reef conservation to climate resilience: Turning Indonesia's marine wealth into global impact
phys-org.description: For Dr. Jamaluddin Jompa, the ocean has never been simply a subject of scientific study. He was born in Takalar, a coastal region of South Sulawesi, Indonesia, and his connection with the sea was forged early. Witnessing the degradation of Indonesia's coastal waters made him wonder: What happens when the ecological relationships that sustain marine ecosystems begin to break down and, more importantly, can they be restored?

phys-org.title: Crystal alignment explains why magnesium alloy plates resist ballistic impacts better in one direction
phys-org.description: Magnesium (Mg) alloys offer a pathway to lighter, more efficient aerospace and defense structures because of their low density, high specific strength and excellent damping capacity. However, their hexagonal close-packed (HCP) crystal structure makes deformation highly dependent on crystallographic orientation.

phys-org.title: Simulated moon soil and recyclable thermoplastics could help build future space infrastructure
phys-org.description: Transporting material from Earth to the moon is an expensive proposition: By some estimates, moving a single kilogram (2.2 pounds) can cost more than $1 million. Any plan to build a permanent human habitat up there will depend on bringing that sky-high cost down.

phys-org.title: Chernobyl particles reveal unexpectedly stable nuclear fuel after 40 years

Analyses show that these "hot particles" are far more stable than had previously been assumed. phys-org.title: Clearer air does not always signal lower harmful potential from particle pollution
phys-org.description: Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) is commonly associated with both health concerns and poor visibility. However, these two effects do not necessarily improve or worsen at the same time.

phys-org.title: Hydrothermal vents supply a geochemical precursor of ATP that could have powered early life
phys-org.description: Where did the energy come from to power the chemical origin of life, and how did phosphate come to be the universal energy currency of cells? Biologists from the Institute of Molecular Evolution at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf (HHU) have uncovered a new source of energy that drove primordial chemical reactions on the early Earth forward to kick-start metabolism. phys-org.title: Researchers uncover the key to driving employee support during organizational changes
phys-org.description: When organizations undergo major shifts, such as restructuring or adopting new working systems, employees often face uncertainty about how to understand and respond to those changes.

phys-org.title: Young infants see saliva sharing as a sign of a close bond, experiments suggest
phys-org.description: Imagine you're an infant. Just a few months in the world, trying to gather your faculties, testing gravity—you're pretty helpless and fully reliant on the people around you. As a result, one of your primary tasks as a new person—even before hand-eye coordination and responding to your own name—is to figure out how the people you've just met are connected to each other.

phys-org.title: Tetrahedral iron can help clays exchange electrons about ten times faster
phys-org.description: Smectites are clay minerals that can contain large amounts of structural iron. Unlike iron oxides, they do not dissolve when their iron is reduced, so they can be reduced and reoxidized many times. This makes them a recyclable pool of redox-active iron that supports microbial respiration, transforms contaminants and influences nutrient and trace element cycling.

phys-org.title: Newly available satellite data show just how flawed some river models can be
phys-org.description: "Is there enough water? What's happening with climate change? How do I operate my hydro plant? In a world of water problems, there are problems that we need a good model to solve," says Colin Gleason, a hydrologist in the Riccio College of Engineering at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. But the models are only as good as the math that they're based on, and short of measuring every river in the world, there is no way to check this on a global scale.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

undark.title: The Embryos That Don’t Come From Eggs and Sperm
undark.description: Human embryo models mimic the earliest development stages; they could offer a glimpse of the first weeks of pregnancy — a mysterious period for which natural embryos are seldom available — and potentially shed light on miscarriage, congenital anomalies, and other health issues. But how far should they go?

undark.title: Book Review: A Contrarian View of How Consciousness Evolved
undark.description: In “Natural Intelligence & the Logic of Consciousness,” neuroscientist Antonio Damasio argues against the conventional theory that consciousness stems from high-level brain function and cognition, which in turn leads to feelings. Instead, he writes, our basest feelings led us to our loftiest thoughts.

undark.title: AI Presents Science with a ‘Ship of Theseus’ Problem
undark.description: Opinion | AI is being integrated into every part of the scientific process, including education, publishing, and the research itself. What does it mean if every component of the enterprise gets replaced by AI tools over time? C. Brandon Ogbunu explores what happens when science gets stripped of human involvement.

undark.title: Interview: What Does the ‘I’ in AI Really Mean?
undark.description: Is it possible that AI is — or might one day become — truly intelligent? Undark posed the question to five experts in linguistics, computer science, cognitive science, and psychology. They offered very different answers, though they agreed that the term “intelligence” is vague and poorly suited to the debate.

proj-syn.title: Why the US-China Trade Truce Matters
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump’s agreement to extend their trade truce reflects the fact that both sides have leverage over the other. In a world where the rules-based trading system is not functioning, the current fragile equilibrium may be the best one can hope for.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Voters Have Moved
proj-syn.description: A strong performance by the right-wing, Donald Trump-aligned candidate in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election demonstrates that the left-wing ruling party has failed to keep up with the times. The Brazilian electorate is older, more devout, and more preoccupied with crime and personal security than it once was.

proj-syn.title: Does Inclusive Finance Really Need Stablecoins?
proj-syn.description: Today, 1.3 billion adults—more than half of them women—remain excluded from the formal financial system, and lower-income consumers still struggle to find and access the financial products and services they need. Contrary to much hype, stablecoins are not the best way to solve either of these problems.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Election Debacle Is Lula’s Fault
proj-syn.description: Brazil's left has just suffered a crushing election defeat and will most likely lose the presidency at the end of October. The causes are many, beginning with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's longstanding refusal to groom an appealing successor.

proj-syn.title: Sino-American Stability Without Trust
proj-syn.description: The main outcomes of the Trump-Xi summit—the two-month trade extension, the dialogue on AI, and even the carefully chosen language on Taiwan—point to Sino-American relations being in a holding pattern. For both sides, the main task is to prevent managed rivalry from devolving into outright confrontation.

proj-syn.title: Iran’s Moment of Opportunity
proj-syn.description: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. But as justified as the Iranian leadership might feel in pursuing an obstinately maximalist strategy, it must be careful not to mistake short-term advantages for longer-term gains.

proj-syn.title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?
proj-syn.description: When Russia replaced the Soviet Union as a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council in 1991, it did not even attempt to follow the process outlined in the UN Charter. Now that Russia’s usurpation of the USSR’s seat has enabled it to wage a war of aggression, the dubious legal status of its position must be revisited.

proj-syn.title: To Support Nepal, Waive Remittance Fees
proj-syn.description: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

proj-syn.title: What a Canada–Europe Alliance Needs
proj-syn.description: With trade, finance, technology, and supply chains having all become instruments of coercion, Canada, Europe, and other likeminded democracies must come together to defend their interests. But strategic convergence between governments is not enough; if a new alliance is to endure, it needs deep roots in society.

proj-syn.title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
proj-syn.description: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

proj-syn.title: Global AI Oversight Now
proj-syn.description: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

proj-syn.title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
proj-syn.description: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

proj-syn.title: Conserving a Connected Ocean
proj-syn.description: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

proj-syn.title: Why Is the Global Economy So Resilient?
proj-syn.description: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

proj-syn.title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
proj-syn.description: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

proj-syn.title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
proj-syn.description: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

proj-syn.title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

proj-syn.title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
proj-syn.description: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.
